newsitem.title: USA: USDA offers Mexico $1.075 bln in GSM-102 for FY97.
newsitem.headline: USDA offers Mexico $1.075 bln in GSM-102 for FY97.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday authorized $1.075 billion in credit guarantees for sales of U.S. farm goods to Mexico under the Export Credit Guarantee Program (GSM-102) for fiscal 1997.
At the same time, the department offered $125 million in credit guarantees for sales of U.S. breeder livestock to Mexico under the long-term program, GSM-103.

The guarantees issued under GSM-103 can cover financing periods of more than three years and up to 10 years, while the GSM-102 program guarantees repayment of short term-loans of 90 days to three years.

Under the GSM-102 program, USDA allocated $500 million for a range of commodities, including corn products, cotton, dairy products, feed grains, fresh fruit, hides, hops, meat, oilseeds, potatoes, poultry breeder stock, rice, wheat, wood products, hay, barley malt, and vegetable oil.
It said specific details for the unallocated $575 million would be issued later.
Sales must be registered by Sept. 30, 1997, with exports no later than Nov. 30 of that year.
